Part (2) follows from part (1) and
Lemma <REF_0001>.
Let us prove part (1).
We first use Algebra, Lemma <REF_0002>.
This lemma implies that if <MATH_0001> is a disjoint union of spectra of finite
separable field extensions of <MATH_0002> then <MATH_0003> is unramified.
Conversely, suppose that <MATH_0004> is unramified.
By Algebra, Lemma <REF_0003> for every <MATH_0005>
the residue field extension <MATH_0006> is
finite separable. Since <MATH_0007> is locally
quasi-finite (Lemma <REF_0004>)
we see that all points of <MATH_0008> are isolated closed points, see
Lemma <REF_0005>.
Thus <MATH_0009> is a discrete space, in particular the disjoint union
of the spectra of its local rings. By
Algebra, Lemma <REF_0006> again these
local rings are fields, and we win.

<STRUCT_0001>
The following lemma characterizes an unramified morphisms as
morphisms locally of finite type with unramified fibres.

Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of schemes.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> If <MATH_0002> is unramified then for any <MATH_0003> the field extension
<MATH_0004> is finite separable.
<STRUCT_0003> If <MATH_0005> is locally of finite type, and for every
<MATH_0006> the fibre <MATH_0007> is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable
field extensions of <MATH_0008> then <MATH_0009> is unramified.
<STRUCT_0004> If <MATH_0010> is locally of finite presentation, and for every
<MATH_0011> the fibre <MATH_0012> is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable
field extensions of <MATH_0013> then <MATH_0014> is G-unramified.
<STRUCT_0005>
